### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **23** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**33** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d62d973734d1e0af3f183340a5674f320b7c0858`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `packageId (4 routes)`
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os validate (command, 81 pages)`
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **45** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d62d973734d1e0af3f183340a5674f320b7c0858` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b371df4db1b448b6ec902d282f9a4d2b3b6231f4` — the merge of head `40dfde1ada0f1de2c6e9d91aacc7c96d0c97baa5` into base `d62d973734d1e0af3f183340a5674f320b7c0858`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b371df4db1b448b6ec902d282f9a4d2b3b6231f4 && git checkout b371df4db1b448b6ec902d282f9a4d2b3b6231f4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d62d973734d1e0af3f183340a5674f320b7c0858 40dfde1ada0f1de2c6e9d91aacc7c96d0c97baa5 && git checkout -B drift-repro d62d973734d1e0af3f183340a5674f320b7c0858 && git merge --no-ff 40dfde1ada0f1de2c6e9d91aacc7c96d0c97baa5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d62d973734d1e0af3f183340a5674f320b7c0858
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d62d973734d1e0af3f183340a5674f320b7c0858` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `40dfde1ada0f1de2c6e9d91aacc7c96d0c97baa5`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-extension-field-suffix.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-gate.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.extension-field-suffix.test.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-extension-field-suffix.test.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/extension-field-suffix.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/extension-field-suffix.test.ts, packages/cli/test/validate-extension-field-suffix.test.ts, packages/cli/test/validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts + packages/spec/src/data/field-customization.ts (`isExtensionFieldName`, `EXTENSION_FIELD_SUFFIX`), packages/spec/src/kernel/customization-package.ts (`isCustomizationPackage`), packages/spec/src/kernel/manifest.zod.ts (`ManifestSchema`), packages/spec/src/api/package-api.zod.ts (`PackageInstallManifestSchema`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-install.ts (`installPackage` parse), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save-door-refusals.ts (`saveWriteBinding`), packages/cli/src/utils/artifact-packages.ts, docs/adr/0146 D10 and decided item 7 — all read on `main`, not reviewed. Not reviewed: `.changeset/28564-extension-field-suffix.md` (prose face, read for ②) and `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` (generated by `check-engine-double-contract.mjs --write`).

Inputs: card #28564 body and its three comments (unblock record, claim, os-dev-report 6560057796), PR #28724 body, file list and net diff against `main` at the merge base `da6f0ce35d`, and the 48 check-runs on the head: 35 success, 13 skipped (UI, docs, dogfood shards and opt-in harnesses), 0 failures. `check:changeset-no-major` and `check:adr-0087-registration` are among the green runs.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged against the cited code:

1. **Public surface widens**: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` index exports `judgeExtensionFieldSuffix`, `extensionFieldSuffixRefusalError`, `objectBodyExtensionFieldSuffixRefusal` and three types (`index.ts:38-41`). Right: the card wants ONE judge, exported, asked by the two doors outside the package; the cli util (`utils/extension-field-suffix.ts`) is not exported from the cli index. No `packages/spec/**` file moves; no new error code; no schema or type changes. Right.
2. **The judge** (`protocol-extension-field-suffix.ts:138-181`): pure, reads `isExtensionFieldName` and `isCustomizationPackage` from the spec and spells neither the suffix nor the pair rule. Case (a) on a non-pair package's own objects and its `objectExtensions`; case (b) on a pair's `objectExtensions[].fields` keys without the suffix; a pair's own objects and an extension of one of them skipped; an empty or non-string `packageId` skipped. Right against D10 and the card's cases. `isCustomizationPackage` is syntactic (some base derives the id) — the judge inherits that from the spec, as it should; `a.custom.custom` is no pair (pinned).
3. **Save door** (`protocol.ts:21626-21637`): asked of every writer in both modes, on `saveWriteBinding`, after the package door (`refusePackagedBaseOverride`, :21158) and the #23165 write-address resolution (:21188), so a publish-mode save naming no package is judged against the package the item resolves into. A draft save naming no package gets binding `null` from `saveWriteBinding` (`protocol-save-door-refusals.ts:655-656`) and is judged at its promotion instead. Right. Envelope `VALIDATION_ERROR` / 400 with `issues[]`, the owner judge's. Right.
4. **Restore** (`protocol-authoring-gate.ts:112-114`, `restoredBodyWriter`): both callers, `rollbackMetaItem` (:27795) and `revertCommit`'s restore limb (:27428), judged on the restore binding. Right. `rollbackToPackageCommit` loops through `revertCommit`, so it is covered; `revertStoredPackage` only discards drafts.
5. **Promotion** (`protocol.ts:23734-23739`, `promoteDraftForPublish`): on `promoteInto`, before `repo.promoteDraft`; both `publishMetaItem` and `publishPackageDrafts` promote through it and the batch aborts (pinned). Right.
6. **`duplicatePackage`** (`protocol.ts:26047-26072`): every active `object` row of the source, renamed per `renameMap`, judged against `request.targetPackageId` before `this.installPackage(dupManifest)`, which the door's own comment identifies as its first mutation. `deepRewrite` never renames a field key outside a reference site, so the judged field names are the written ones. Refused whole, 400, nothing minted (pinned). Right.
7. **`os validate`** step 3a-iv (`validate.ts:694-720`, `utils/extension-field-suffix.ts:38-51`): each `packages[]` entry under its own id (via `artifactPackages`), else the stack under `manifest.id`; exit 1 in both output modes, rows carry `path`, `code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR'`, `rule`, `packageId`, `message`. A stack naming no id is not judged, which follows the judge's own rule. Right. The parity ledger records `findExtensionFieldSuffixRefusals` under `VALIDATE_ONLY_GATES` with its reason: right, since the card and D10 item 7 name publish, validate and install, not `os build`.
8. **Marketplace `handleInstall`** step 1c'' (`marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:1813-1849`): after 1c' (dependency check), before 1e (install mode), 1d, `manifestService.register` (:2144) and every `ledger.write` (:2205, :2258), so a refused artifact registers, writes and ledgers nothing on the managed and the unmanaged branch (pinned: `registered` and `ledger` both empty, `installMode: 'unmanaged'` refused). Each `packages[]` entry under `manifestIdOf(entry.manifest)`, the body otherwise. Answer `422 VALIDATION_ERROR` with `details.refusals`, the door's existing unrunnable-code envelope. Right.
9. **`installPackage` gets no call** (seat-accepted reading). Verified on `main`: `PackageInstallManifestSchema` is `ManifestSchema.extend({scope})` (`package-api.zod.ts:229`), `ManifestSchema` is a `strictObject` (`manifest.zod.ts:485`) whose `objects` is `z.array(z.string())` (:727) and which has no `objectExtensions` key; `installPackage` parses with it at `protocol-package-install.ts:230` before any write. A field body is refused 400 at the parse (pinned, mp test section 5, registry never written). ADR-0146 D10 names `installPackage` as the install door by path; the reading that its closed manifest IS the refusal is right, and the pin keeps it honest if the manifest ever opens. Right.
10. **Case (b) only at validate and `handleInstall`** (seat-accepted reading). Right: the save, restore and promotion doors take `object` bodies through `objectBodyExtensionFieldSuffixRefusal`, which judges the body as the package's own object, and `duplicatePackage` copies `object` rows; `objectExtensions` arrive only in a whole package body. The runtime `object_extension` write door is #28574's.
11. **A write bound to no package is not judged** (judge line 139, pinned at the save door: `probe_env` with `x__c` stored active, binding `null`). Right against the card ("given a package id", case (a) "in a package that is not a `.custom` pair") and D11 ("a package-less row for an item no package ships is environment metadata"); the leak it leaves is named in ④.
12. The judge also reads a `fields` array of `{ name }` entries. It reads that dialect to refuse, never to admit, so it is no consumer-side alias in the Prime Directive #12 sense. Right.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset: `minor` on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, the three packages the diff moves; BREAKING banner; one ADR-0087 marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, with the measured count (0 fields) as the migration note; `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`. AGENTS.md rule 3: a kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves, `(narrowing)` is BREAKING and carries its disposition. Matches what the diff publishes. Right.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, identical on the PR body and the changeset. `clause2-line.mjs` reads this spelling as "a diff that widens one surface and narrows another; both facts are true and both are read". Both facts hold here: the public surface widens (the six new exports from the metadata-protocol index, judgment ①.1) and the accept set narrows (every door). `no (narrowing)` would answer the 扩大公开面 half falsely. The card prescribed this exact line. The arm is right and must not change. Both CI readers of the line are green on the head.
- No `skip-changeset`; three released packages publish. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions[0]` (should `os build` run the judge, as #28643 made it run the override gate): option A taken; follow-up #28727 is open on the board with the title naming the gap; the parity ledger row names the same gap in the tree. Answered.
- `out_of_scope_findings[0]` (the same gap, carrier seat 1): covered by #28727. Answered.
- Dev flags in the report: the one merge conflict in `validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts` (#28681 had emptied `VALIDATE_ONLY_GATES`; this branch keeps one row) — resolved in the tree as described, the docblock rewritten to match. `check:engine-double-contract` first read 1, green after `--write` (the pinned json hunk is that write). `check:type-check-debt` first read 3 behind the branch's own lock, 0 on re-run; the head's check-run is green. No flag left open.
- Serial constraint from the claim: `protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts` is not in the file list. Held.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real. On `main`, `EXTENSION_FIELD_SUFFIX` and `isExtensionFieldName` (`field-customization.ts:33-45`) are declared and read by no door, and D10 item 7 says the suffix "is refused outside `.custom` at publish, at `os validate` and at the install door". No declared capability is taken away at a consumer: the count on `main` is 0 affected fields; a `.custom` pair's `region__c` is admitted at every door and a vendor extension's plain field is admitted (ADR-0029 D7 kept), both pinned per door. Each door keeps its own envelope; no code is minted; no spec file moves.

Break attempts, in the tree:

- **A door that can still land `x__c` outside a pair — found, should-fix.** The save door admits `x__c` into a package-unbound row (judgment ①.11, pinned). `POST /api/v1/packages/:id/adopt-orphans` → `reassignOrphanedMetadata` (`protocol.ts:26610-26720`) then rebinds every active unbound row into the target package by a storage update plus `applyRegistryWriteThrough` (:26706-26713), asking no judge — so that row's `x__c` field becomes a plain package's own. The door is not among the card's named doors, and it asks neither the namespace-prefix nor the owner judge either (a pre-existing class, not this PR's), and D11's close of the package-less write shrinks its input; a follow-up card for the adopt door (the three body-against-address judges in one call) is the right shape. Not a must-fix: the card's judge is defined over a package id, and the leak needs a row the card's own rule admits.
- **Unmanaged marketplace install of a `.custom` artifact**: judged at 1c'' under the pair id (admitted), then `importUnmanagedPackage` copies every item through `saveMetaItem` with `packageId: targetPackageId` (`protocol.ts:26472-26477`), so the save door judges it again against the new base, all-or-nothing. Holds.
- **Duplicate from a pair into a plain id**: refused before `installPackage` (first mutation); from a plain package into a pair id: the pair's own objects, not judged. Holds.
- **Promotion ordering on sealed managed content — should-fix, minor.** The two blocks above the new one (`protocol.ts:23660`, :23696) are gated `!this.isSealedManagedItem(...)` so a sealed row gets the store's one refusal (`NOT_OVERRIDABLE`); the suffix block is not, so a sealed object draft carrying `x__c` would be told "rename the field" first. The save door refuses such a draft before it exists (`refusePackagedBaseOverride` at :21158 precedes the judge), so the branch is hard to reach; gate it the same way for one-row-one-refusal consistency when next touched.
- **A `packages[]` artifact's top-level `objects`** are not judged at validate or install — the same reading `findOverrideDeclarationRefusals` and the dependency check (1c') take; consistent, no second dialect.
- **A pair extension of the pair's own object** is skipped only when the object is in the same body; at the active doors the pair's objects are never judged, so no false refusal. Holds.
- Case (b)'s prescription names `fieldPatches`, which exists on `main` (`object.zod.ts:4849-4857`). Message under the 500-character cap. `extensionFieldSuffixRefusalError`'s `first!` is guarded by every caller's length check.

No must-fix.
